items.rationale: Sections 5.2.6–5.2.7 cover necessary dismantling and refitting for access or drying, provided it is not billed again as labour. Case 46 supports €90 for the service.
Section 5.2.7 covers the drying period supported by moisture readings. The stated two-week run is consistent with the seven days billed, for which the reference estimate is €313.
Section 7.4.4 bars an unexplained surcharge without an itemised materials list. The €39 estimate applies only if the contractor substantiates the necessary materials.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(c) allow one standard mineral-wool shell in the original diameter if needed to make good the affected pipe area. The reference estimate is €26.
Section 5.2.2 allows only the first charge for disposal of the same debris, measured by the actual volume. The drying invoice is listed first, and €60 is consistent with Case 46.
Section 5.2.6 covers levelling the affected substrate before the tiles are replaced. The comparable Case 46 material allowance is €38.
Section 5.2.6 covers necessary preparation of the affected wall, but sections 3.5(d) and 7.4.1 exclude overlap with levelling or separately billed labour. If distinct, €30 per m² gives about €83.
Section 5.2.6 expressly covers a necessary service opening in the damage area. The comparable single opening in Case 46 supports €18.50.

The format meets section 7.14(d), but sections 3.5(a), 3.5(e) and 7.1.6 limit the allowance to comparable standard tiles for the affected area, with reasonable cutting waste. Using Case 46’s roughly €52 per m² for about 3.2 m² including waste gives about €167.

The tiles exceed the 90 × 90 cm limit in section 7.14(d), triggering section 3.5(f); the separate standard tile line also leaves no basis for a second allowance. The €167 figure applies only if this line is accepted instead as the sole standard-equivalent tile charge.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(a) cover finishing the repaired area with standard sanitary silicone. At about €13 per metre, 3.6 metres gives €47.
Section 7.4.2 permits the first travel charge per contractor per document. This is the only such charge on the tiling invoice, and the reference estimate is €81.
Section 7.4.1 covers necessary hours at customary rates, excluding labour already included in other lines. The 14-hour prior is €1,239, close to Case 46’s €1,260 tested amount.

items.description: Remove basement drywall and insulation wool
items.rationale: Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.6 cover necessary removal in the affected basement, but section 7.4.4 requires supporting itemisation for the combined flat rate. If documented, comparable removal allowances total about €95, excluding separately billed waste disposal.

items.description: Remove damp plaster in basement rooms
items.rationale: Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.5 cover removal only where basement plaster was affected by the leak. The single-unit reference allowance is €29.

Sections 3.5(b) and 7.1.5 exclude work outside the established damage area, and the attic removal is expressly unrelated. The €29 estimate applies only if a comparable affected patch were independently documented.
Sections 3.5(d) and 5.2.2 exclude the second charge for the same disposal already billed at position 5. The €60 reference estimate applies only if this were shown to be the first eligible charge.
